findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_prediction_history" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Time series for a prediction market the desk polls (top ~100 by 24h volume on Polymarket + Kalshi, snapshots every ~15 min): YES price and 24h volume points, wi…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.detail: Description of "chat_post" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_fx_rates, get_my_portfolio, get_updown_markets, get_updown_history, chat_read, chat_teams · Private data: get_updown_history, enter_competition, chat_post · Public sink: get_fundamentals, place_order, get_insider_trades, claim_referral_code, chat_post, get_my_referrals.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_fx_rates, get_my_portfolio, get_updown_markets, get_updown_history, chat_read, chat_teams · Private data: get_updown_history, enter_competition, chat_post · Public sink: get_fundamentals, place_order, get_insider_trades, claim_referral_code, chat_post, get_my_referrals

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
